Finding a recording no longer depends on remembering where you filed it. The library could only be browsed a folder at a time — no node meant "everything", and past the home screen's six most recent the only way in was to click through folders one by one. That put the entire burden on filing, which is precisely the thing people forget.

There is now an "所有錄音" node above the folders, and it reads down a calendar rather than across a grid. A folder answers "what is in here", and a card carrying a title, a snippet and four stats is the right shape for that question. This node answers a different one — what did I sit through lately — and that is scanned rather than browsed: rows gathered under 今天, 昨天, 本週稍早 and then by month, each carrying the folder it lives in, with roughly twice as many meetings on screen at once. Moving, sharing, renaming and deleting all work from here as well, because filing something you have just found is most of the point of a view that spans every folder.

⌘K is the other half of the same problem. Browsing is aim-and-click: you have to know where a thing lives before you can reach it, and the library's search box only helps once you have already picked the scope it searches. The palette opens over the whole tree at once — folders, the fixed nodes, organizations and their shared folders, and every recording by title — so something you can already name costs one keystroke and a couple of letters instead of three deliberate acts. ↑↓ moves, ↵ lands, and an empty query lists the tree rather than showing a blank box. Every row is a place, never an action: ↵ on a highlighted row can only navigate, because a palette that mixes destinations and verbs turns ↵ into a gamble over a list your finger is already scrolling.

The live transcript has stopped dragging you back to the bottom. It scrolled to the tail every time a segment arrived — every few seconds, for the whole meeting — so scrolling up to re-read something said a minute ago was impossible: the view was pulled away mid-sentence. It now follows the tail only while you are already standing at it. Scroll up and the transcript keeps appending below without moving your view; scroll back down and it picks the follow up again, and a "回到最新" pill offers the way back in one click. Dragging the scrollbar counts as taking over, exactly as a wheel or a swipe does, and jumping to a timestamp from the debrief still lands where you asked and stays there. The coach feed follows the same rule.

An agent can now reach the recordings that are not on this device. Parley Cloud already mirrors an account's recordings across its devices, but MCP could only read local disk, so an agent on a secondary machine was blind to everything recorded elsewhere until somebody clicked the card in the library. list_cloud_recordings returns the account's cloud mirror and tags each entry with where it stands here — recorded elsewhere and not pulled down yet, a local copy that has fallen behind, or in step — and download_cloud_recording fetches one: transcript, saved analysis, and the audio when the cloud copy has it. Afterwards it is an ordinary local recording, listed and readable and replayable like any other. The two calls that pull a whole recording also got a deadline that fits the work, so a slow connection no longer reports failure while the download is still running.
